To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LC and VTA are distinct sources of dopamine in the hippocampal formation, that the LC dopamine system is critical for memory consolidation of distinct novel events, and that the LC dopamine and noradrenaline systems are both required for memory persistence of distinct novel events.
the LC, a brain region that is critical for arousal, attention and learning, is also a source of dopamine that promotes memory consolidation.
distinct novelty activates LC dopaminergic neurons to promote memory retention and that common novelty activates VTA dopaminergic neurons for systems memory consolidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes novelty and the neural mechanisms that underlie the persistence of novel experiences.
the mechanisms by which the brain processes and stores memories, and how the brain can be modulated to improve memory performance.
how the brain processes and remembers new information and how the brain adapts to the changing world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
distinct novelty and common novelty are two distinct types of novelty that activate two distinct dopaminergic pathways in the hippocampus to promote memory persistence.
the VTA and LC systems play complementary roles in the consolidation of distinct and common novelty, respectively.
the LC and the VTA are two distinct dopamine systems that promote memory persistence via two different pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two dopamine systems are complementary to each other and together promote memory persistence.
the VTA-LC axis is a key neural substrate for novelty detection and memory persistence.
the two systems, the VTA and LC, are differentially activated by common and distinct novelty and that their dopamine projections to the hippocampus promote distinct memory persistence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the LC and the VTA play complementary roles in memory persistence, and that their distinct contributions may be due in part to the differential sensitivity of their projections to the dopamine D1 receptor.
distinct novelty and common novelty are processed by distinct neural systems, which are differentially modulated by dopamine and noradrenaline.
dopamine released from the VTA is critical for semantic memory formation, whereas dopamine released from the LC plays a key role in memory consolidation of distinct novelty.
